newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire's Mobutu expected in France for short stay.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu expected in France for short stay.

text.p: Ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko was expected at his French Riviera holiday mansion on Friday, leaving Zaire again as proximity talks were reported in South Africa between his representatives and rebels holding a region of eastern Zaire.

French officials said Mobutu's private plane was expected to arrive at Nice airport between 5.00 and 6.00 p.m. (1600 GMT and 1700 GMT) from Gbadolite, his hometown in conflict-striken Zaire. He was expected to stay in France for four days.
Mobutu, who was underwent surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland in August and convalesced at his French residence, returned to France for three weeks last month for medical tests.
It was not immediately known if he would meet French or other envoys while at the coastal mansion in Roquebrune Cap-Martin as he did during previous stays.
Several African leaders came to consult him about the crisis in Zaire where rebels backed by Rwanda and Uganda have taken a wide swathe of territory in the east of the country.

In Cape Town, a U.S. embassy official confirmed that South Africa was leading proximity talks in a search for peace in Zaire, where the government has intensified air raids against rebel strongholds, and U.S. assistant secretary of state for African affairs George Moose was there to help.

South African officials remained silent about progress towards a face-to-face meeting in Cape Town between representatives of Mobutu's government and the Zaire rebel movement headed by Laurent Kabila.
They declined to comment on a statement in New York by United Nations spokesman Fred Eckhard that Kabila was expected in Cape Town by the weekend.
Ngbanda Nzambo Ko Ayumba, Mobutu's nephew and chief security adviser who has been in Cape Town since Sunday, has played down the idea of peace talks in South Africa.
He told Radio France International in a telephone interview from Cape Town on Thursday that Zaire had pre-conditions for any talks and said there would be no meeting in South Africa.

"We are being attacked by three neighbouring countries and we demand that the three neighbouring countries pull out their soldiers and let Zaireans find a solution to their internal problems," Ngbanda said.

Zaire says forces from Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi invaded its territory in support of Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms in October, accusing Zaire of denying them citizenship and preparing to expel them.
